item.title: Two children remain under observationat CWM after Civic House electrical incident
item.description: Two children remain under observation at CWM Hospital after suffering electrical flash burns during an incident at Civic House in Suva. The children, aged 6 and 13, are receiving medical treatment following the incident on Wednesday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
Two children remain under observation at CWM Hospital after suffering electrical flash burns during an incident at Civic House in Suva.

The children, aged 6 and 13, are receiving medical treatment following the incident on Wednesday afternoon.

The Ministry of Employment, Productivity and Workplace Relations has launched an Occupational Health and Safety investigation to determine the cause of the electrical fault and the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The Ministry says preliminary findings indicate that an electrical fault occurred inside the building’s ground-floor main switchboard room at about 3.20pm.

Employment Minister Agni Deo Singh says some electrical components in the switchboard were found to have sustained heat damage.

However, the exact cause of the fault remains under investigation.

The affected switchboard has been shut down, with access restricted to authorised repair and inspection personnel.

A Prohibition Notice has also been issued to the Suva City Council as the owner of Civic House.

The Ministry says electricity should not be restored until the electrical system has been fully inspected and cleared by the relevant authorities.

Singh says the safety of workers, visitors and members of the public must always come first.

item.title: 4 girls allegedly trafficked in two separate domestic trafficking cases
item.description: Four girls are alleged to have been trafficked in two separate domestic human trafficking cases, with the case files now with the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions. Police say in the first case, two suspects are alleged to have subjected a young girl to domestic trafficking in Labasa.
item.content:encoded:
Four girls are alleged to have been trafficked in two separate domestic human trafficking cases, with the case files now with the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

Police say in the first case, two suspects are alleged to have subjected a young girl to domestic trafficking in Labasa.

Police say the investigation has been completed and the file was forwarded to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions on 6th June 2026 for an independent legal review.

The second case was reported at the Lautoka Police Station and involves one of the two suspects from the Labasa case.

The suspect is alleged to have subjected three girls to domestic trafficking in the Western Division.

Police say two police officers were also questioned in relation to the case.

The investigation has been completed and the file was forwarded to the ODPP on 31st August.

Police say as part of their broader investigative approach, the Anti-Money Laundering Unit is now looking into possible financial crime offences involving proceeds that may have arisen from the alleged domestic trafficking.

item.content:encoded:
What should have been a morning filled entirely with excitement was an emotional one for 28-year-old Kaitalo Voce, who spent an hour crying and remembering her late son before getting ready for one of the biggest milestones of her life, her graduation.

Voce, who graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Management, says the occasion was bittersweet as her young son who was her biggest motvation, was not there to witness one of her biggest achievements after passing away last Monday following an illness.

She says graduating today meant much more than receiving a qualification, it marks the culmination of a journey in which she balanced her studies with motherhood, family responsibilities and personal loss, with her son remaining one of her greatest motivations.

Insert: We have been through a lot 10th Sept

Speaking to fijivillage News about her journey, the 28-year-old from Vivili Village in Savusavu says while studying, she would deliberately choose afternoon classes so she could spend the first part of the day looking after her son.

Voce says managing her time allowed her to continue her studies while fulfilling her responsibilities as a mother.

She says her road to graduation was filled with many challenges, from losing her dad to her father-in-law and then her son. However, she says the support of her husband and family kept her going.

The new graduate encourages others not to give up when their own journey becomes difficult or to become discouraged if achieving their goals takes longer than expected.

She says everyone has their own journey and their hard work will eventually pay off.

item.title: Police officer sentenced to 14 years and nine months for raping 15-year-old girl
item.description: A 44-year-old police officer has been sentenced to 14 years and nine months in prison for raping and sexually assaulting his wife’s 15-year-old cousin between 2019 and 2021. The girl had been staying with the police officer during school holidays.
item.content:encoded:
A 44-year-old police officer has been sentenced to 14 years and nine months in prison for raping and sexually assaulting his wife’s 15-year-old cousin between 2019 and 2021.

The girl had been staying with the police officer during school holidays.

He was found guilty of three counts of rape and fou r counts of sexual assault .

In sentencing, Suva High Court Judge Justice Dane Tuiqereqere noted that the man was a first offender and had previously been a man of good character.

Justice Tuiqereqere said the girl had lost confidence and now has difficulty trusting people as a result of the offences.

Justice Tuiqereqere says the police officer was supposed to provide the 15-year-old with a safe space to stay.

Justice Tuiqereqere says the officer had led an exemplary life, however, all the good he had done was undone when he committed the offences.

The man will be eligible for parole after serving 10 years and nine months .

He has 30 days to appeal the sentencing.

item.description: As 61 people have taken their own lives this year compared to 63 in the same period last year, Empower Pacific has highlighted the importance of strengthening early identification, accessible mental health and psychosocial support, family and community support, and timely referral for people experiencing distress or crisis. item.content:encoded:
As 61 people have taken their own lives this year compared to 63 in the same period last year, Empower Pacific has highlighted the importance of strengthening early identification, accessible mental health and psychosocial support, family and community support, and timely referral for people experiencing distress or crisis.

Empower Pacific confirms that f rom 1st January to 31st July this year, they have provided counselling and social work support to 169 individuals who had attempted suicide or engaged in deliberate self-harm.

They say of these, 137 individuals sought counselling support for attempted suicide and deliberate self-harm, out of which 32 individuals also sought social work support.

A total of 110 individuals who received counselling support following attempted suicide were recorded, including 46 males, 63 females and one female person with a disability.

The highest number of counselling cases was recorded among those aged 18 to 25 years, followed by those aged until 17 years.

Women and girls aged 18 to 25 years recorded the highest number of attempted suicide cases.

Empower Pacific Chief Executive Officer Patrick Morgan says s uicide is influenced by multiple and often interconnected factors rather than one single cause.

He says based on Empower Pacific's data, some of the challenges identified by the individuals include relationship and family difficulties, domestic violence, prolonged stress, alcohol and other drug use, mental health concerns, grief and loss, trauma, health concerns, work andschool-related pressures, and socioeconomic and financial difficulties.

Morgan says Fiji continues to face gaps in specialist mental health resources and access to services.

He says WHO reports that Fiji has a low specialist mental health workforce, with geographical remoteness and limited transportation also creating challenges in accessing services.

Morgan says WHO identifies strengthening and decentralising mental health services, increasing workforce capacity, and training non-specialist health-care providers as important priorities.

Morgam says t here is also a need to strengthen public awareness and reduce stigma and discrimination as it can discourage people from seeking or accepting the help they need.

He says some warning signs may include withdrawing from family and friends, significant changes in mood or behaviour, expressing feelings of hopelessness or being a burden, increased substance use, giving away valued belongings, or talking about death or not wanting to live.

The CEO stresses that prevention starts with noticing changes, asking directly and compassionately if someone is struggling, listening without judgement, and helping them connect with appropriate support.

Morgam says people who appear to be at immediate risk should not be left alone and should be connected with urgent professional or emergency support.

He also emphasises that suicide prevention is a shared responsibility and a simple conversation, early support and a safe connection to appropriate services can make a difference.

If you or someone you know is struggling, Empower Pacific’s 24/7 toll-free counselling helpline, 5626, is available for support.
